rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate all eight peaks and identify critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. This scouting run establishes the elution window for subsequent gradient trimming and selectivity tests.

Lengthen only the gradient to determine which crowded pairs respond to slope. The first run's short elution time leaves room to improve resolution while keeping the final peak near the unpenalized 10-minute window.
Keep the improved gradient slope and raise temperature to test selectivity at the remaining near-coelution. Higher temperature should also create time headroom for further resolution improvements.

Slightly flatten the gradient at the best temperature to spread the remaining critical pair. The current last peak at 8.56 minutes leaves enough headroom for this extension without an expected time penalty.

The longer gradient worsened the critical pair, so reverse direction and test a shorter gradient. This should improve that pair and reduce elution time, while checking whether the earlier pair currently at R = 1.61 remains adequately resolved.

Use the 20-minute gradient to resolve the early cluster, with a modest temperature reduction to shift the later critical pair away from coelution. This tests a selectivity compromise between the 40 and 60 °C results while retaining time headroom.

Retain the best temperature and gradient duration, but slightly narrow the gradient window to tune the two nearly limiting pairs. The higher starting organic fraction should also shorten retention, with the first peak sufficiently retained to justify this small increase.

Slightly flatten injection 7's slope by lowering the endpoint and shortening the programmed gradient together. This should improve both early critical pairs while preserving the later pair's resolution margin; the endpoint remains well above the observed elution window.

Fine-tune the slope from 0.04583 to 0.045 organic fraction per minute to lift the early limiting pairs above R = 1.5. The later critical pair has a small resolution margin, and the endpoint remains above the last peak's estimated elution fraction.

Injection 9 achieves the maximum CRF and remains the benchmark. Test a higher starting organic fraction with a shallower slope to seek a shorter fully resolved separation while monitoring the three marginal pairs.

Slightly flatten injection 10's slope to test whether the early critical pair can recover resolution while retaining its shorter elution time. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution fraction; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

The 60 °C refinements show competing resolution limits, so test a substantially different temperature for an alternative selectivity pattern. A steeper gradient and higher endpoint should limit the added retention at lower temperature; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.
Lengthen only the gradient to determine whether the low-temperature near-coelution responds to slope. Most other pairs have resolution headroom, and the last peak should remain within 10 minutes.

Reduce the gradient slope slightly to push the remaining slope-responsive pair above R = 1.5. The last peak is expected to remain below 10 minutes, potentially yielding a second maximum-score method with more resolution margin.

Raise temperature one step from the fully resolved low-temperature method to shorten retention while testing whether its resolution margins survive. Injection 9 remains the faster maximum-score benchmark.

Return to the fully resolved 25 °C selectivity and raise the starting organic fraction one step to shorten retention. The resulting shallower slope may help preserve the critical pair's resolution as the elution window shifts earlier.

Raise the starting organic fraction again while reducing the slope enough to help preserve the marginal critical pair. This tests a shorter elution window at the successful low-temperature selectivity; injection 9 remains the fastest maximum-score method.

Test whether a moderate temperature increase resolves injection 17's remaining close pair while shortening retention. The earlier temperature comparison showed strong selectivity changes, so this run will also check for new coelutions after peak reordering.

Keep the gradient fixed and test 45 °C to see whether the crowded cluster separates beyond the 35 °C selectivity crossover. This explores a potentially faster separation while retaining injection 9 as the proven maximum-score method.

Flatten the gradient at 45 °C to test whether the two early critical pairs can reach baseline resolution. The last peak at 6.23 minutes provides substantial time headroom, potentially allowing full resolution before the 7.45-minute benchmark.

Raise temperature one step to test selectivity at the close pairs identified in injection 20 while shortening retention. Keep the gradient fixed to isolate the temperature effect; injection 9 remains the proven maximum-score benchmark.

Return to the best temperature and starting composition, testing a shallower gradient that ends shortly before the last peak and continues as a hold. This should improve the early limiting pairs while testing whether the changed late-elution regime preserves full resolution; injection 9 remains the maximum-score benchmark.

Test the highest temperature with the narrowed, shallow gradient to see whether its selectivity changes recover resolution beyond the 50 °C crossover. This offers a potentially faster alternative, while injection 9 remains the proven maximum-score method.

Test a slightly shallower slope than injection 9 to measure the resolution margin around the best method. The early critical pairs should improve, while the later limiting pair will determine whether full resolution is retained; the maximum CRF has already been achieved.

Use the final injection to test whether an early transition to an isocratic hold improves the crowded cluster through different selectivity. This is exploratory rather than a predicted improvement; injection 9 already achieves the maximum CRF and remains the recommended method unless this run is fully resolved and faster.
